forbidden_overclaims: Exact deaths, economic losses, or countrywide damaged-asset totals.
Treating compact AOI receptor files as representative of all Peru and Ecuador.
Treating off-event CHIRPS, ERA5, WorldPop, OSM, catalog search, or preview imagery as direct proof of local flood severity.
Claiming ENSO alone proves local impacts without the locked Peru/Ecuador flooding anchor.

key_findings: Peak ONI reaches 2.4 C in OND 1997 and remains at or above 1.5 C for eight event-window seasons.
SOI is negative for 11 event-window months and strongly negative for 9 months, supporting ocean-atmosphere coupling.
The locked event anchor identifies Peru/Ecuador flooding, so the briefing should prioritize flood preparedness rather than drought, wildfire, or monitoring-only handling.

notes: Off-event local precipitation, WorldPop, OSM, HDX, EONET, and preview imagery are not used in this ground truth.
The local hazard statement comes from the locked Peru/Ecuador flooding event anchor; quantitative support comes from ONI and SOI indices.

reasoning_requirements: Classify the event as a coupled climate-to-coastal-flood preparedness problem, not a generic climate-index monitoring case.
Use ONI magnitude/persistence and SOI coupling as quantitative climate-driver evidence.
Use the locked event anchor for the Peru/Ecuador flooding hazard statement instead of off-event local precipitation or receptor files.
Reject drought, wildfire/catalog, and monitoring-only pathways unless the flooding anchor is absent.

criteria.description: Gives the ENSO-amplified Peru/Ecuador coastal flood-preparedness pathway and assigns high priority.
full_credit: Uses enso_amplified_coastal_flood_preparedness_priority or a semantically equivalent label.
Sets priority to high or clearly indicates high initial flood preparedness priority.
criteria.name: Final answer and priority
partial_credit: Names ENSO flooding but omits priority.
Gives high priority but uses an overly generic climate label.

criteria.description: Uses ONI magnitude and persistence as the large-scale climate-driver anchor.
full_credit: Mentions peak ONI near 2.4 C in OND 1997.
Mentions sustained warm ENSO across about eight seasons at or above 1.5 C.
criteria.name: ENSO magnitude and persistence
partial_credit: Identifies a strong El Nino without quantitative support.
Provides one correct ONI metric but misses persistence.

criteria.description: Uses the pressure-coupling signal to support the mechanism.
full_credit: Cites mostly negative SOI, about 11 negative months, or 9 strongly negative months.
Explains that SOI supports coupled ocean-atmosphere behavior.
criteria.name: Ocean-atmosphere coupling
partial_credit: Mentions SOI without explaining its role.
Recognizes atmospheric coupling but gives no quantitative anchor.

criteria.description: Uses the locked event anchor to connect the climate driver to Peru/Ecuador flooding without relying on off-event local rainfall products.
full_credit: Mentions the locked Peru/Ecuador flooding event framing.
Treats the flooding anchor as the local hazard statement and does not substitute off-event AOI rainfall.
criteria.name: Peru/Ecuador flooding anchor
partial_credit: Mentions Peru/Ecuador flooding but does not distinguish it from climate monitoring.
Uses the anchor weakly or with unsupported local rainfall claims.

criteria.description: Rejects drought, vegetation stress, wildfire/catalog monitoring, and monitoring-only pathways.
full_credit: Explains why strong ENSO plus flooding anchor favors flood preparedness.
Does not overstate exact losses or countrywide damaged-asset totals.
criteria.name: Distractor rejection
partial_credit: Generally avoids overclaims but leaves one ambiguous statement.

criteria.description: Returns concise valid JSON in the requested structure with answer, mechanism_chain, three key_findings, and priority.
full_credit: Includes exactly the requested high-level fields and three useful findings.
criteria.name: Output structure
partial_credit: Mostly follows the requested structure but has minor formatting or concision issues.
